newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq rises after Greenspan eases concerns.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq rises after Greenspan eases concerns.

text.p: Nasdaq shares rose Wednesday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said monetary policy was not a tool to manipulate the stock market.

Nasdaq shares showed immediate gains after Greenspan's testimony eased investor concerns. The Nasdaq composite index ended the day at 1329.09, up 11.72 points or 0.89 percent. Dow industrials surged 93.13 points to 6945.85.
"It's a Greenspan market. He said negative things last week and rocked the market. He was more middle of the road today, and the market voted in favor of what he had to say," one trader said.

In other news, Corporate Express Inc crumbled 8-3/16 to 10-1/8 after a dismal fourth quarter forecast. Broderbund Software Inc also sank 7-3/8 to 23-1/8 after it warned its second quarter profits would fall short of Wall Stret estimates.

Some large capitalization technology companies also showed improvement after Merrill Lynch said the drop in semiconductor stock prices was close to ending. Intel Corp added 3-1/8 to 149-1/2. Microsoft Corp gained 1-3/4 to 100-7/8. Overall, advancing issues beat decliners 2369 to 1886 on total volume of about 673 million shares.
